text: OneLake underlies Fabric IQ as the unifying layer across clouds and on-premises sources, using shortcuts, mirroring, and the OneLake catalog so the same governed data grounds semantic models, ontologies, and agents.

sources.title: What is Fabric IQ? - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
sources.summary: Microsoft Learn's conceptual introduction to Fabric IQ, the new Fabric workload that turns raw OneLake data into shared business meaning (via semantic models and an ontology item) so that people and AI agents can reason about customers, shipments, and other business concepts consistently. It also positions Fabric IQ inside the broader 'Microsoft IQ' enterprise-intelligence layer alongside Work IQ, Foundry IQ, and Web IQ, and inventories the Fabric items that make up the IQ (preview) workload.
takeaways: Fabric IQ is one of four pillars of 'Microsoft IQ' (with Work IQ, Foundry IQ, Web IQ), and its specific job is supplying business-entity and data context.
Two Fabric items anchor Fabric IQ: the existing Power BI semantic model (curated analytics layer) and the new ontology (preview) item (business vocabulary, relationships, rules, actions).
Ontologies can be generated/aligned directly from existing semantic models, so production BI investments can bootstrap the ontology rather than starting from scratch.

The IQ (preview) workload bundles several items beyond ontology and semantic model: Plan (preview), Graph, Data agent, and Operations agent (preview) — most of which are shared with other Fabric workloads.
OneLake remains the unifying data substrate underneath Fabric IQ even though it is not formally listed as an IQ workload item.

text: A shortcut is an embedded reference inside OneLake that points at another file-store location, giving workloads access to external operational data without copying it or building ETL pipelines, and it can be combined with cross-tenant data sharing for governed external access.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric terminology

text: OneLake is Fabric's single logical data lake, built on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, and every Fabric compute experience comes preconfigured to use it as its native store — analogous to Office apps automatically using the organization's OneDrive.

sources.title: What is Microsoft Fabric? (Microsoft Fabric overview)

text: OneLake shortcuts mount existing external storage such as Azure Data Lake Storage, Amazon S3, and Google Cloud Storage as zero-copy references, so cross-cloud data can be analyzed in Fabric without ETL or migration.

sources.title: What is Microsoft Fabric? (Microsoft Fabric overview)

text: A OneLake shortcut is an object that points from a shortcut path to a target path in another storage location; it behaves like a symbolic link, so deleting the shortcut leaves the target untouched, while moving, renaming, or deleting the target can break the shortcut.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: Shortcuts can be created in lakehouses and KQL databases, either interactively in the Fabric portal or programmatically through the OneLake shortcuts REST API.

sources.title: Unify data sources with OneLake shortcuts - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake shortcuts give a lakehouse live, read-only references to data held elsewhere in OneLake, in external systems, or even in other tenants via cross-tenant data sharing, avoiding duplication of the underlying data.

sources.title: What is a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?

text: Every Microsoft Fabric tenant is provisioned with exactly one OneLake; tenants cannot create additional OneLake instances or delete the existing one, and no separate storage resources need to be provisioned or managed.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: All Fabric data items, including lakehouses and warehouses, automatically persist their tabular data in OneLake using the open Delta Parquet format, regardless of which engine wrote the data.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake shortcuts are references to data held in other locations, within the same workspace, across workspaces, or outside OneLake in stores like ADLS, Amazon S3, or Dataverse, and they make remote files and folders appear as if stored locally, enabling virtual data products without duplication.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake soft delete retains deleted files for seven days, and soft-deleted files can be restored with Azure Storage Explorer or PowerShell, providing protection against accidental deletion.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake security operates on two planes: control plane permissions decide what users can do in the environment (create, manage, share items), while data plane permissions, the OneLake security model, decide what data users can read; control plane grants often confer data access by default.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Permissions in OneLake follow the storage hierarchy of workspace, item, and folder (such as Tables/ and Files/), with lower levels inheriting from the parent item or workspace by default; of the four workspace roles, Admin, Member, and Contributor can read and write OneLake data, while Viewer cannot read OneLake data unless explicitly granted access through OneLake security roles.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake file explorer for Windows lets users browse all workspaces and data items and upload, download, or edit files from the desktop, making the data lake usable by non-technical business users.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: OneLake authenticates exclusively with Microsoft Entra ID for both users and service principals, mapping the extracted identity onto Fabric-defined permissions; service principal use requires a tenant administrator to enable SPNs tenant-wide or for specific security groups.

sources.title: Simplifying secure data access with Delegated OneLake Shortcuts (Preview)
sources.summary: Fabric Updates Blog post introducing Delegated OneLake Shortcuts as a preview auth option layered on top of the shortcut model already documented in this KB. The new material is the formal delegated-identity connection method for OneLake-to-OneLake and cross-tenant shortcuts, and how it differs from External Data Sharing - not the base mechanics of shortcuts, which onelake-shortcuts.json already covers.
takeaways: Delegated OneLake Shortcuts are a preview feature that adds an optional delegated-identity authentication mode to shortcut creation, alongside the existing default pass-through mode.
The delegated identity can be an organizational account, a service principal, or a workspace identity, and is configured once on the shortcut connection rather than per consumer.
Delegated shortcuts now explicitly support cross-tenant scenarios, letting one Fabric tenant shortcut to OneLake data in another tenant through a configured identity.

Delegated shortcuts are positioned as distinct from External Data Sharing: delegated shortcuts assume the consumer already has an identity in the producer's tenant, while External Data Sharing is for consumers with no identity there.

text: The delegated identity attached to a shortcut can be an organizational account, a service principal, or a workspace identity, and choosing delegation is optional per shortcut; shortcuts default to pass-through authentication unless delegation is explicitly selected at creation time.

sources.title: ServiceNow Zero-Copy Querying of Enterprise Data in Microsoft OneLake (Preview)
sources.summary: Fabric Updates Blog post announcing a ServiceNow Workflow Data Fabric connector that reads OneLake data directly through Iceberg-compatible table APIs. The angle for Atlas readers is what the integration says about OneLake's open-standards query surface, not the ServiceNow product pitch itself.
takeaways: OneLake now has at least one named operational-SaaS consumer (ServiceNow) reading data in place via open table APIs, not a proprietary connector.
The integration is explicitly built on the Apache Iceberg REST Catalog standard rather than a Fabric-specific protocol.
This is a preview-stage feature as of the post's publication, not yet generally available.
The same open API surface is described as usable by other engines (Trino, DuckDB, Spark), positioning OneLake as a multi-engine data foundation rather than a Fabric-only store.

text: This ServiceNow OneLake connector is called out as a preview capability at time of publication, not a generally available feature.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg vs Delta Lake Comparison
sources.summary: A 2026 comparison of Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake table formats, covering their differing metadata architectures, the two formats' recent convergence efforts, and how OneLake exposes cross-format interoperability for Fabric lakehouses.
takeaways: Iceberg and Delta Lake both write data as Parquet but track table state through different metadata mechanisms, which is why cross-format reads require translation rather than being trivial.
OneLake provides three distinct mechanisms for Iceberg interoperability, not just one, each suited to different integration scenarios.

Fabric lakehouses remain natively Delta-format, so Iceberg support is about letting external engines and Iceberg-native tables interoperate with OneLake, not a format change for Fabric-created tables.
The broader ecosystem (Delta UniForm, Iceberg v3) is converging toward mutual readability, which reduces the cost of picking either format as a starting point.

text: After assigning a OneLake security read role on a shortcut path, the post reports an observed propagation delay of roughly two to three minutes before access takes effect.

sources.title: OneLake Shortcut Authorization Failed: Fixing Cross-Workspace 403 Errors
sources.summary: A community troubleshooting walkthrough for a 403 'OneLake shortcut authorization failed' error that appears when a lakehouse shortcut spans two workspaces. It maps the error to three distinct root causes and gives a matching fix for each.
takeaways: A 403 on a cross-workspace OneLake shortcut is often an identity-mode misconfiguration, not a missing permission.
Control-plane workspace roles (e.g. Viewer) and OneLake data-plane security roles are separate grants; both must be present.
Row-level security can produce a 403-looking preview failure in the UI even when the underlying query succeeds.
External ADLS Gen2 shortcuts have their own credential-expiry failure mode, distinct from internal OneLake shortcuts.

text: The post describes OneLake gaining native support for both Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg table formats, enabling bidirectional access with Iceberg-managed tables from other platforms.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric Overview: Microsoft Fabric Tutorial Series
sources.summary: An independent tutorial-series overview walking through Fabric's workload lineup, OneLake storage model, compute engines, and a snapshot of platform news as of mid-2026, aimed at readers getting oriented on the whole suite rather than one workload.
takeaways: OneLake shortcuts can virtualize data across multiple clouds (not just Azure), which changes how architects think about avoiding data movement/egress.
OneLake is gaining native multi-format support (Delta and Iceberg side by side), which matters for interoperability with non-Fabric lakehouse stacks.
Storage lifecycle tiering is coming to OneLake, but blanket cooling policies risk breaking Delta table reads if applied incorrectly.
Direct Lake's performance promise is conditional — it silently degrades to DirectQuery under several common conditions that teams should monitor for.
The P-SKU to F-SKU capacity migration has firm deadlines that make delaying capacity planning risky for legacy Premium customers.

text: Rayfin routes application data into OneLake as part of its managed deployment, without requiring a separate ETL pipeline to move transactional data into the analytics layer.

sources.title: Microsoft Rayfin: Guide to Fabric Apps
sources.summary: An independent explainer on Rayfin, an open-source SDK/CLI announced at Microsoft Build 2026 that provisions a governed, code-first application backend (SQL database, auth, GraphQL API, static hosting) directly onto Microsoft Fabric capacity, underpinning the broader Fabric Apps initiative.
takeaways: Rayfin is a code-first CLI/SDK, not a low-code tool — it targets professional developers and AI coding agents, positioned distinctly from Power Apps.

A single deploy command provisions three managed child services: a SQL Database with schema generated from TypeScript decorators, Entra ID authentication, and OneLake-connected static content hosting.
Application data lands in OneLake automatically as part of the deployment model, without a separate ETL step to get transactional data into the analytics estate.
The product was in public preview at the time of the post, with the author explicitly flagging that CLI syntax and APIs are subject to change before general availability.

Rayfin requires an active Fabric capacity (a minimum tier for development, a higher tier recommended for production) plus tenant-admin enablement, tying it into existing Fabric capacity administration.

text: OneLake shortcuts can virtualize data from other clouds' object stores (e.g., S3-compatible and other cloud blob storage) as well as other ADLS Gen2 accounts and Fabric Lakehouses, letting Fabric reference that data without physically copying it.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric security fundamentals
sources.summary: Vendor architectural overview of Fabric's security model aimed at admins: how the SaaS platform separates metadata and compute, how authentication and authorization flow through Microsoft Entra ID and signed tokens, how data residency and multi-geo work, and how data is protected at rest and in transit.
takeaways: Fabric is SaaS-first: platform security, compliance, and governance are largely built in rather than something admins must independently stand up, unlike traditional PaaS data platforms.
Two distinct planes exist: a metadata platform holding tenant metadata (in the tenant's home region) and a back-end capacity platform doing compute and storing customer data (in the capacity region).
Authentication is delegated entirely to Microsoft Entra ID, including support for conditional access policies and service principals.

Data residency is controlled by where the tenant's metadata cluster and workspace capacities are placed, with Multi-Geo capacities as the mechanism for storing/processing data outside the home region.
Workspaces are the primary OneLake security boundary, with item-level permissions layered on top for finer-grained access.

sources.summary: Microsoft Learn's conceptual introduction to Fabric IQ, the new Fabric workload that turns raw OneLake data into shared business meaning (via semantic models and an ontology item) so that people and AI agents can reason about customers, shipments, and other business concepts consistently. It also positions Fabric IQ inside the broader 'Microsoft IQ' enterprise-intelligence layer alongside Work IQ, Foundry IQ, and Web IQ, and inventories the Fabric items that make up the IQ (preview) workload.
takeaways: Fabric IQ is one of four pillars of 'Microsoft IQ' (with Work IQ, Foundry IQ, Web IQ), and its specific job is supplying business-entity and data context.
Two Fabric items anchor Fabric IQ: the existing Power BI semantic model (curated analytics layer) and the new ontology (preview) item (business vocabulary, relationships, rules, actions).
Ontologies can be generated/aligned directly from existing semantic models, so production BI investments can bootstrap the ontology rather than starting from scratch.

The IQ (preview) workload bundles several items beyond ontology and semantic model: Plan (preview), Graph, Data agent, and Operations agent (preview) — most of which are shared with other Fabric workloads.
OneLake remains the unifying data substrate underneath Fabric IQ even though it is not formally listed as an IQ workload item.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric terminology

text: OneLake security operates on two planes: control plane permissions decide what users can do in the environment (create, manage, share items), while data plane permissions, the OneLake security model, decide what data users can read; control plane grants often confer data access by default.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Permissions in OneLake follow the storage hierarchy of workspace, item, and folder (such as Tables/ and Files/), with lower levels inheriting from the parent item or workspace by default; of the four workspace roles, Admin, Member, and Contributor can read and write OneLake data, while Viewer cannot read OneLake data unless explicitly granted access through OneLake security roles.

sources.title: OneLake data security overview - Microsoft Fabric

text: Every Microsoft Fabric tenant is provisioned with exactly one OneLake; tenants cannot create additional OneLake instances or delete the existing one, and no separate storage resources need to be provisioned or managed.

sources.title: OneLake, the OneDrive for data - Microsoft Fabric

text: A OneLake shortcut is an object that points from a shortcut path to a target path in another storage location; it behaves like a symbolic link, so deleting the shortcut leaves the target untouched, while moving, renaming, or deleting the target can break the shortcut.

sources.title: Microsoft Fabric Overview: Microsoft Fabric Tutorial Series
sources.summary: An independent tutorial-series overview walking through Fabric's workload lineup, OneLake storage model, compute engines, and a snapshot of platform news as of mid-2026, aimed at readers getting oriented on the whole suite rather than one workload.
takeaways: OneLake shortcuts can virtualize data across multiple clouds (not just Azure), which changes how architects think about avoiding data movement/egress.
OneLake is gaining native multi-format support (Delta and Iceberg side by side), which matters for interoperability with non-Fabric lakehouse stacks.
Storage lifecycle tiering is coming to OneLake, but blanket cooling policies risk breaking Delta table reads if applied incorrectly.
Direct Lake's performance promise is conditional — it silently degrades to DirectQuery under several common conditions that teams should monitor for.
The P-SKU to F-SKU capacity migration has firm deadlines that make delaying capacity planning risky for legacy Premium customers.

sources.title: Apache Iceberg vs Delta Lake Comparison
sources.summary: A 2026 comparison of Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake table formats, covering their differing metadata architectures, the two formats' recent convergence efforts, and how OneLake exposes cross-format interoperability for Fabric lakehouses.
takeaways: Iceberg and Delta Lake both write data as Parquet but track table state through different metadata mechanisms, which is why cross-format reads require translation rather than being trivial.
OneLake provides three distinct mechanisms for Iceberg interoperability, not just one, each suited to different integration scenarios.

Fabric lakehouses remain natively Delta-format, so Iceberg support is about letting external engines and Iceberg-native tables interoperate with OneLake, not a format change for Fabric-created tables.
The broader ecosystem (Delta UniForm, Iceberg v3) is converging toward mutual readability, which reduces the cost of picking either format as a starting point.

text: After assigning a OneLake security read role on a shortcut path, the post reports an observed propagation delay of roughly two to three minutes before access takes effect.

sources.title: OneLake Shortcut Authorization Failed: Fixing Cross-Workspace 403 Errors
sources.summary: A community troubleshooting walkthrough for a 403 'OneLake shortcut authorization failed' error that appears when a lakehouse shortcut spans two workspaces. It maps the error to three distinct root causes and gives a matching fix for each.
takeaways: A 403 on a cross-workspace OneLake shortcut is often an identity-mode misconfiguration, not a missing permission.
Control-plane workspace roles (e.g. Viewer) and OneLake data-plane security roles are separate grants; both must be present.
Row-level security can produce a 403-looking preview failure in the UI even when the underlying query succeeds.
External ADLS Gen2 shortcuts have their own credential-expiry failure mode, distinct from internal OneLake shortcuts.

text: Rayfin routes application data into OneLake as part of its managed deployment, without requiring a separate ETL pipeline to move transactional data into the analytics layer.

sources.title: Microsoft Rayfin: Guide to Fabric Apps
sources.summary: An independent explainer on Rayfin, an open-source SDK/CLI announced at Microsoft Build 2026 that provisions a governed, code-first application backend (SQL database, auth, GraphQL API, static hosting) directly onto Microsoft Fabric capacity, underpinning the broader Fabric Apps initiative.
takeaways: Rayfin is a code-first CLI/SDK, not a low-code tool — it targets professional developers and AI coding agents, positioned distinctly from Power Apps.

A single deploy command provisions three managed child services: a SQL Database with schema generated from TypeScript decorators, Entra ID authentication, and OneLake-connected static content hosting.
Application data lands in OneLake automatically as part of the deployment model, without a separate ETL step to get transactional data into the analytics estate.
The product was in public preview at the time of the post, with the author explicitly flagging that CLI syntax and APIs are subject to change before general availability.

Rayfin requires an active Fabric capacity (a minimum tier for development, a higher tier recommended for production) plus tenant-admin enablement, tying it into existing Fabric capacity administration.
